content.text:
Netlist and Micron Enter Patent License and Settlement Agreements: The release says Netlist and Micron agreed to settle and mutually release pending proceedings between them, and that Micron would receive a five-year license covering Netlist patents including server DIMM and HBM technologies. It states fees of $30 million per quarter from Q4 2026 through Q3 2031, totaling $600 million. Its safe-harbor text identifies litigation, collection, and performance risks. (time=2026-10-06T12:00:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Netlist, Inc. Form 8-K: The current SEC page describes agreements dated October 5, including a worldwide five-year license, quarterly fees, a separate purchase of 10 million Netlist shares for $1 million, and forward-looking risks. The exact EDGAR acceptance time and a pre-cutoff copy were not verified; these additional filing details are not treated as established public facts by the cutoff. (time=UNKNOWN; cutoff=UNKNOWN).
USITC Institutes Section 337 Investigation of Certain Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) Devices, Products Containing the Same, and Components Thereof (III): The USITC said it instituted investigation 337-TA-1523 based on Netlist’s August 11 complaint and August 25 supplement, and identified Micron among the respondents. Netlist requested exclusion and cease-and-desist orders. The Commission expressly said institution was not a decision on the merits. (time=2026-09-23; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
NETLIST, INC. v. MICRON TECHNOLOGY, INC., No. 24-1707 (Fed. Cir. 2026): The dated opinion says the Federal Circuit affirmed the PTAB’s conclusion that all challenged claims of Netlist’s ’339 patent were unpatentable as obvious in the appeal involving Micron. This is a specific patent/IPR matter, not a ruling on all Netlist–Micron disputes. (time=2026-09-02; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
